title: scratch.resize can shrink a split neighbour's panes until they vanish
body:
`Layout::resize_to` in `decade-ui/src/panes.rs` (added in 4392ac1 for `scratch.resize`, decade-4c3de8) sets new ratios only on the splits along the path to the resized pane. A neighbour that is itself split keeps its inner ratios, so its panes shrink in proportion. `room` only guarantees that each neighbour as a whole stays at its minimum, and `arrange_node` gives any pane under `MIN_PANE` an empty rectangle, so it vanishes.

A review probe on 100 columns with the layout `[0 | [1 | [2 | 3]]]` at 0.5 ratios ran `resize_to(0, (100, 40))` and got columns `[88, 6, 0, 0]`. Panes 2 and 3 disappeared. The docs and changelog say neighbours shrink "down to their smallest". A split neighbour with an uneven ratio, such as `[1|2]` at 0.2 shrunk to its 8-column minimum, loses pane 1 the same way.

## Proposal

When `resize_to` takes room from a split neighbour, it sets that neighbour's inner ratios so every pane inside stays at least `MIN_PANE`, or it limits `room` to what proportional shrinking keeps at that minimum. Add the probe's layout as a test.
